extracted.intended_audience: apprenticeship program sponsors, Registration Agencies, State Apprenticeship Agencies (SAAs), employers, intermediaries, workforce boards, and other National Apprenticeship System stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts the proposed regulatory definitions, duties, and procedural standards in the DOL's NPRM revising 29 CFR part 29, including requirements for program design, data/reporting, reviews, and transitions. Intended to guide sponsors, SAAs, and Registration Agencies on compliance and program structure under the proposed rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-apprenticeship program definition and required elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines 'pre-apprenticeship program' to align parts 29 and 30 and WIOA; includes access to educational and career counseling, supportive services, and opportunities to earn industry-recognized credentials; participants in pre-apprenticeship are not 'apprentices' under these regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose is to ensure consistent usage across parts 29 and 30 and to allow sponsors to report efficacy under proposed §29.25; programs should form written partnerships with registered apprenticeship sponsors and have equitable, intentional, achievable strategies to recruit, hire, and retain individuals from underserved communities; may include work-based learning (job shadowing, internships) and support pipelines into CTE and registered apprenticeship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Proficiency means the demonstrated, measurable attainment by an apprentice of each relevant job skill and competency necessary to perform successfully at the journeyworker level in a given occupation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition clarifies that attainment of individual competencies culminates in overall occupational proficiency for subpart A purposes; used to assess completion/outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program review (replaces quality assurance assessment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Program review is the administrative process by which OA assesses whether programs are in full compliance with registered apprenticeship regulations in parts 29 and 30.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program reviews may include provision of technical assistance to help a sponsor achieve full compliance; adding a definition clarifies expectations in communications with Department or SAA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program standards adoption agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: A written agreement reached outside of collective bargaining between a sponsor that has developed standards of apprenticeship and a Participating Employer that agrees to utilize and adhere to those standards for training apprentices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies mechanism for employers to adopt sponsor standards where not governed by collective bargaining.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional registration (revised)
rubrics_metrics.description: Retains provisional registration concept with changes: replaces 'rescinded' with 'deregistered' and removes '1-year' to align provisional period with the first full training cycle; cross-reference updated to the entire part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes that provisional registration involves compliance reviews across all of parts 29 and 30 and clarifies administrative terminology and timing under proposed §29.10.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognized postsecondary credential (definition and components)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines recognized postsecondary credential for registered apprenticeship to include: industry-recognized certificate or certification; a Certificate of Completion (required to be administered/provided upon program completion); a Federal/State/local occupational license where required; or an associate or baccalaureate degree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aligns with WIOA; intended for use as a programmatic outcome and for assessing credential attainment for program/system reporting under proposed §29.25; apprentices may attain multiple such credentials and interim credentials (obtained during participation) are encompassed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registered apprenticeship program (new comprehensive definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Replaces 'apprenticeship program' with 'registered apprenticeship program' requiring minimum duration and consisting of both paid on-the-job training (OJT) and related instruction, and being registered by a Registration Agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies baseline structural elements sponsors must include for registration and distinguishes registered programs from pre-apprenticeship and CTE models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registered CTE apprenticeship program
rubrics_metrics.description: A registered CTE apprenticeship is a model registered under subpart B embedded within a CTE program that includes structured integrated education and career training and a paid OJT component; admits CTE apprentices with CTE apprenticeship agreements approved by a Registration Agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires a minimum of 540 hours of CTE apprenticeship-related instruction (at least 12 postsecondary credit hours); distinct from subpart A registered apprenticeship (which requires no less than an average of 144 hours per 2,000 OJT hours under proposed §29.7(b)(4)); not a substitute for subpart A but sponsors are encouraged to align standards where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration Agency must be a governmental entity
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed revision capitalizes 'Agency' and clarifies that a Registration Agency must be a governmental entity tasked with registering apprenticeship programs and conducting program reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replaces older references to 'reviews for compliance' and 'quality assurance assessments' with the defined 'program reviews' (assessments for compliance with parts 29 and 30).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of Apprenticeship
rubrics_metrics.description: Defined as the organized, written plan containing the terms and conditions of employment, training, and supervision within a given registered apprenticeship program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These standards apply to registered apprenticeship programs and their required contents are discussed in proposed §29.8.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related instruction (retained distinction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Retains existing definition of related instruction and affirms it is distinct from on-the-job training within a registered apprenticeship program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintains the separate instructional component sponsors must provide in addition to OJT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive services (definition and examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adds 'supportive services' aligned with WIOA sec. 3: services necessary to enable an individual to participate in apprenticeship, such as transportation, childcare, dependent care, housing, needs-related payments, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists non-exhaustive examples including linkages to community services, educational testing assistance, referrals for physical/mental health care, assistance with uniforms/tools, assistance with books/school supplies, payments/fees for applications/tests/certifications, legal aid; may be provided by intermediaries, local workforce boards, and coordinated with career/training services under WIOA sec. 134(d)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical assistance (redefined)
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical assistance refers to any support provided to help an entity (program sponsor or SAA) satisfy the requirements of parts 29 and 30, not just assistance to remedy nonconformity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes technical assistance as proactive and ongoing (e.g., written resources, guides, increased staffing, improved forums/portals) to assist in program setup, compliance questions, or responses to new developments; OA plans proactive, comprehensive TA campaign and targeted support for data reporting in proposed §§29.25 and 29.28.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work process schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines 'work process schedule' as a training plan that establishes a series of measurable competency benchmarks whose acquisition by the apprentice should lead to occupational proficiency by the conclusion of the apprenticeship term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies a previously omitted definition to ensure consistent use across the regulations and to tie schedules to measurable competencies and proficiency outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Underserved communities (definition and purpose)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adds definition derived from Good Jobs Principles, protected bases in 29 CFR part 30, and WIOA populations; used throughout the proposed rule to target strategies for recruiting and retaining individuals from these communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department seeks comments on the definition and on embedding recruitment/retention strategies; definition underpins DEIA and outreach expectations for sponsors and SAAs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of Apprenticeship (OA) roles and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: OA is the administrative and coordinating entity of the National Apprenticeship System, responsible for implementing the NAA, approving registered apprenticeship programs/standards as a Registration Agency, recognizing SAAs, promoting industry-validated standards, maintaining National Apprenticeship System data, promoting DEIA, providing technical assistance, and engaging stakeholders domestically and internationally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed §29.3(a)-(i) details OA's duties including formulating/updating regulations, issuing subregulatory guidance, managing resources and recognition programs, convening industry, and coordinating TA and data reporting; OA will maintain data to support §§29.25 and 29.8 and to enable disaggregated analysis for equitable outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation to other laws and collective bargaining
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.4 clarifies that part 29 does not invalidate or supersede any Federal, State, or local law or collective bargaining agreement that establishes more protective or stringent minimum labor standards of apprenticeship; part 29 establishes a floor, not a ceiling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where higher standards exist in law or contracts, those higher standards control; Department encourages programs to exceed minimums to develop high-quality training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Severability
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes a severability provision: if any provision or portion of part 29 is declared invalid by a court, other provisions capable of operating without the invalidated portion remain in effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard safeguard to preserve enforceable parts of the rule if some parts are struck down.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition provisions (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposes reasonable transition periods to allow orderly implementation of amended regulations, balancing stakeholder burdens with the goal of strengthening the National Apprenticeship System.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department solicits comments on necessity, length, and additional transition provisions and wants input from applicants for suitability determinations, program sponsors, labor organizations, SAAs, and other affected stakeholders on feasibility and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition timelines for occupations' suitability (§29.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed transition schedule for applicability of updated suitability requirements in §29.7: potential occupations (not previously determined suitable) — requirements apply 90 days after final rule effective date; existing suitable occupations (Administrator-recognized) and SAA-approved occupations — requirements apply 4 years after effective date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During transition, existing §29.4 requirements remain in effect for potential occupations until the 90-day period; table summarizes scenarios and timelines to promote clarity for applicants and sponsors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essential quality elements for the National Apprenticeship System
rubrics_metrics.description: Identifies the essential quality elements the Department seeks through the rule: approving occupations' suitability, registering apprenticeship programs, approving work process schedules, enhancing worker protections in apprenticeship agreements, and enhancing data and performance reporting/measuring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These elements are the focus of modernization efforts and are the subject of proposed transition provisions and data collection/reporting changes in §§29.25 and 29.28.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim credential clarification
rubrics_metrics.description: Modifies the definition of 'interim credential' to be those recognized postsecondary credentials obtained during an apprentice's participation in a registered apprenticeship program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Links interim credentials to the broader recognized postsecondary credential definition and to reporting/credential attainment measures under proposed §29.25; Department invites comments on alignment with WIOA credential measures and DOL's role in providing interim credentials.
